title: Pathology viva: gastric cancer and Helicobacter pylori

header.contentArea: Pathology: gastric adenocarcinoma, H. pylori, staging and management principles
guidelineVersions: NICE NG83 (published 24 January 2018; last updated 4 July 2023)
Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer guidelines (Lancet Oncol, 2020)

related.why: The oesophageal and junctional counterpart, where PET-CT is routine for radical candidates
Blood supply of the stomach, which defines the nodal stations removed at gastrectomy

brief.scenario: Mr Douglas Marchbank, 68, has a gastric antral ulcer with rolled edges at endoscopy. Biopsies show adenocarcinoma and the urease test is positive for Helicobacter pylori.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the role of H. pylori, the pathology of gastric cancer, and how it is staged and treated.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Cause, type, stage, treat: H. pylori to Lauren type, then CT and laparoscopy, then MDT treatment.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Borrowing the oesophageal pathway: PET-CT for everyone and laparoscopy only sometimes. In gastric cancer it is the reverse.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "H. pylori is a Group 1 carcinogen: chronic gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, cancer."

grid.label: Role of H. pylori
grid.fail: Says only that it is 'linked' to cancer, or that it causes cancer directly without an inflammatory sequence.
grid.pass: Chronic active gastritis progressing to atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia and intestinal-type adenocarcinoma. Classified as a Group 1 carcinogen.
grid.high: Names the sequence as the Correa cascade and adds that H. pylori also underlies gastric MALT lymphoma.

grid.label: Other risk factors
grid.fail: Cannot name risk factors beyond H. pylori.
grid.pass: Smoking, high-salt and smoked or preserved foods, pernicious anaemia (atrophic gastritis), previous partial gastrectomy.
grid.high: Adds family history and hereditary diffuse gastric cancer from germline CDH1 (E-cadherin) variants, managed by genetic referral.

grid.label: Lauren classification
grid.pass: Intestinal type: gland-forming, follows H. pylori and intestinal metaplasia. Diffuse type: poorly cohesive, signet ring cells, infiltrates the wall.
grid.high: Diffuse type affects younger patients, spreads submucosally (linitis plastica), reflects E-cadherin loss and carries a worse prognosis.

grid.label: Staging pathway
grid.fail: Sends every patient for PET-CT, or omits staging laparoscopy.
grid.pass: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis, then staging laparoscopy for every potentially curable gastric cancer to find peritoneal disease.
grid.high: Endoscopic ultrasound and PET-CT only if they would change management; PET-CT when metastases are suspected but unconfirmed.

grid.label: Curative treatment
grid.fail: Proceeds straight to gastrectomy without MDT discussion or perioperative chemotherapy.
grid.pass: Specialist MDT. Chemotherapy before and after surgery, then subtotal or total gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy in a specialist unit.
grid.high: Names FLOT as four cycles before and four after surgery; chemotherapy after surgery considered if none was given before.

grid.label: Advanced disease
grid.fail: Offers resection to a patient with peritoneal or distant metastases.
grid.pass: Metastatic or unresectable disease: palliative systemic therapy in fit patients, best supportive care otherwise.
grid.high: Requests HER2 testing in advanced adenocarcinoma, since HER2-positive disease can receive trastuzumab with chemotherapy.

grid.label: H. pylori and family
grid.fail: Ignores the positive H. pylori result.
grid.pass: Treats his H. pylori infection and confirms eradication.
grid.high: Offers H. pylori testing to first-degree relatives, and genetic referral if the family history suggests hereditary diffuse cancer.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What is the role of H. pylori here?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's linked to stomach cancer somehow.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Spicy food and stress, I think.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure. Is it a staging system?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: CT and a PET-CT. Laparoscopy isn't usually needed if the CT is clear.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: CT shows no metastases. What next?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd book him for a gastrectomy straight away.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd still resect the primary to get the tumour out.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What is the role of H. pylori?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It causes chronic active gastritis, which can progress through atrophy and intestinal metaplasia to dysplasia and adenocarcinoma. It's a Group 1 carcinogen.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Smoking, a high-salt or smoked diet, pernicious anaemia and previous partial gastrectomy.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Intestinal type forms glands and follows H. pylori and metaplasia. Diffuse type is poorly cohesive, with signet ring cells infiltrating the wall.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, then a staging laparoscopy, because CT misses peritoneal disease and he is potentially curable.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Specialist MDT. Chemotherapy before and after surgery, and a subtotal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy for this distal tumour.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: No resection. Palliative chemotherapy if he's fit enough, otherwise best supportive care.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd treat his H. pylori and confirm eradication.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It drives the Correa cascade: gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, then intestinal-type cancer. It is also behind gastric MALT lymphoma.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: He mentions his brother had stomach cancer at 38.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That raises hereditary diffuse gastric cancer from a germline CDH1 variant. I'd refer the family to clinical genetics.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How does the diffuse type behave?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It affects younger patients, spreads under the mucosa and can give a linitis plastica. It reflects loss of E-cadherin and has a worse prognosis.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Should he have PET-CT and EUS?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Only if the result would change management. For gastric cancer PET-CT is for suspected but unconfirmed metastases. The laparoscopy is what every curable patient needs.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: FLOT: four two-weekly cycles before surgery and four after. If he went straight to surgery, I'd consider chemotherapy afterwards.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd request HER2 testing, because HER2-positive adenocarcinoma can have trastuzumab with chemotherapy.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd also offer H. pylori testing to his first-degree relatives.

failures.move: Using PET-CT for everyone and skipping laparoscopy after a clear CT.
failures.consequence: Peritoneal disease is missed and he has a gastrectomy that cannot cure him.

failures.move: Going straight to gastrectomy without MDT or perioperative chemotherapy.
failures.consequence: He loses the survival benefit that chemotherapy adds to surgery.
Major surgery with no survival gain, delaying palliative treatment.

failures.move: Ignoring the positive H. pylori result.
failures.consequence: The infection persists and relatives at risk are not tested.

recovery.when: You mix up the gastric and oesophageal staging pathways
recovery.line: In gastric cancer, laparoscopy is for every curable patient; PET-CT is selective.

recovery.when: Asked for a percentage you are unsure of
recovery.line: I wouldn't quote a figure I can't source; it is a Group 1 carcinogen and the main risk factor.

knowledge.fact: H. pylori: Group 1 carcinogen; gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, cancer.
Lauren: intestinal (glandular, H. pylori) versus diffuse (signet ring, younger, worse prognosis).
Germline CDH1 variants cause hereditary diffuse gastric cancer.
Staging: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis; staging laparoscopy for all potentially curable gastric cancer; EUS and PET-CT only if they change management.
Resectable disease: chemotherapy before and after surgery; consider D2 lymphadenectomy.
HER2 testing in advanced oesophago-gastric adenocarcinoma.
H. pylori eradication reduces gastric cancer risk.

recall.think: Hidden peritoneal disease makes a gastrectomy pointless.
recall.say: "Potentially curable, so CT then staging laparoscopy, and MDT."
do: Perioperative chemotherapy, then gastrectomy with D2 nodes

numbers.meaning: FLOT cycles before and after surgery

recall.trap: A clear CT does not exclude peritoneal disease.
recall.finish: Gastrectomy in a specialist unit; eradicate H. pylori; test relatives.

partner.opening: This man has a biopsy-proven gastric adenocarcinoma and a positive urease test. What is the role of H. pylori?

reveals.finding: His brother died of stomach cancer aged 38.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks for the CT result
reveals.finding: Distal gastric tumour with perigastric nodes. No liver or lung metastases.

push.question: How does H. pylori cause cancer?
push.expect: Gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, cancer; Group 1 carcinogen.

push.question: Describe the two Lauren types.
push.expect: Intestinal glandular versus diffuse signet ring; diffuse worse prognosis.

push.question: CT is clear. Can he go to theatre?
What is the treatment plan?
push.expect: MDT; perioperative chemotherapy; gastrectomy with D2 nodes.

push.question: Is there anything to do about the H. pylori?
push.expect: Eradicate and confirm; test first-degree relatives.

curveballs.prompt: What percentage of gastric cancers are caused by H. pylori?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Declines to quote an unsourced figure; states it is a Group 1 carcinogen and the main risk factor.
Not resectable for cure: MDT, palliative systemic therapy if fit, HER2 testing.
Only if metastases are suspected but unconfirmed and it would change management.
